## Overview

CPython, the reference implementation of the Python programming language, now officially supports the RISC-V architecture as a Tier 3 platform, according to a [Python Insider blog post](https://blog.python.org/2026/08/riscv-now-officially-supported) by core contributor Stan Ulbrych. The milestone, reported by [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/riscv-cpython/), formalizes RISC-V's place in [PEP 11](https://peps.python.org/pep-0011/), the document that governs which platforms ...

editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three source snapshots in sources/2026-09/cpython-adds-risc-v-as-an-officially-supported-tier-3-platform/ from disk (source-0.html.gz = blog.python.org, source-1.html.gz = peps.python.org/pep-0011, source-2.html.gz = infoq.com). Confirmed verbatim in source-0.html.gz: 'RISC-V is now officially supported by CPython as a tier 3 platform', 'quadruple by 2032', 'Ludovic Henry' (x2), 'Sovereign Tech Agency'. Confirmed source-1.html.gz contains the 'riscv64-unknown-linux-gnu' target triple entry. Confirmed source-2.html.gz page title is 'CPython Officially Adds RISC-V Support As a Tier 3 Platform - InfoQ' with 29 mentions of RISC-V and 23 of CPython in body text. All claims, quotes, and specifics in the submission trace correctly to their cited sources — no hallucination or misattribution found.
editor_notes.suspicious_pattern_review: The automated scan flagged source-2.html.gz (InfoQ) for pattern 'system-prompt-reference'. I opened the flagged excerpt in the decompressed snapshot and confirmed via `gunzip -c source-2.html.gz | grep -o '.{200}Shopify Introduces Gisting.{200}'` that the matched text is: '..."imageStoragePath":null,"topicsIds":null,"date":1788465600000,"url":"/news/2026/09/spotify-gisting-llm-performance","title":"Shopify Introduces Gisting: Compressing LLM System Prompts into Learned Tokens","authorsList":["Sergio De Simone"],"itemPath":"/news/2026/09/spotify-gisting-llm-performance"...'. This is a JSON payload for InfoQ's own 'related articles' widget, listing the headline of an unrelated, legitimate InfoQ news story about LLM system-prompt compression technology (Shopify/gisting). It contains no imperative language and does not address an AI agent — it is a false positive from the coarse regex net matching the phrase 'System Prompts' inside an article title, not a prompt-injection attempt. I am overriding the automated REJECT basis tied to this finding; it does not affect the substantive editorial decision below.
